acceptance_criteria.criterion: snapshotIndexMetadata() returns an empty array when index.json does not exist
snapshotIndexMetadata() correctly extracts all metadata keys (excluding episode and url) from an existing index.json
mergePreservedMetadata() correctly merges stored metadata back into $this->indexEntries after a re-fetch
Freshly fetched data (keys already present in an entry) is never overwritten by mergePreservedMetadata()
Methods are private and not part of the public interface

summary: Both private methods implemented in BaseComicSource.php: snapshotIndexMetadata() reads index.json and builds episodeID to metadata map (excluding episode/url keys); mergePreservedMetadata() iterates indexEntries and merges preserved keys without overwriting freshly fetched values. Both are private and not in the public interface.

All 5 acceptance criteria verified. 14 targeted tests and 28 full-suite tests pass with zero regressions. One PHPUnit deprecation notice is a framework-level issue unrelated to the implementation. Both private methods confirmed as private in source. Edge cases (missing episode key, empty preserved map, no matching episodeID) handled correctly in code.

metrics.test_coverage: AC1-AC5 fully covered via 14 dedicated assertions across tests 1-4 plus visibility check

comments.note: One PHPUnit deprecation notice present across all test runs — unrelated to this WP. Framework-level issue for a future upgrade.

summary: Code review passed. Both private methods (snapshotIndexMetadata, mergePreservedMetadata) are correctly implemented, well-scoped, and follow established project patterns. Ordering in fetchIndex is correct: snapshot before reset, merge after _fetchIndex and before autoPopulateFromEpisodes. Two non-blocking suggestions recorded.

comments.note: mergePreservedMetadata accesses $entry['episode'] without a null-coalescing fallback, unlike the symmetrical handling in snapshotIndexMetadata. Adding '$episodeID = $entry["episode"] ?? null; if ($episodeID === null) continue;' would be defensively consistent, even though it's safe in practice because registerEpisode always sets this key.

snapshotIndexMetadata correctly uses the null-coalescing operator on the 'episode' key before using it as a map key — good defensive coding. The !empty($metadata) guard is intentional and correct (entries with only episode/url keys have nothing worth preserving); a brief inline comment would clarify this for future maintainers.

mergePreservedMetadata uses array_key_exists instead of isset — the correct choice to avoid accidentally overwriting a freshly-fetched explicit null value. Both reference loops (here and in autoPopulateFromEpisodes) correctly unset($entry) after the loop.

summary: Added inline comment in snapshotIndexMetadata() before the !empty($metadata) guard to clarify that entries with only episode/url keys have nothing worth preserving (per WP-001 code-review gold-nugget). PHPDoc blocks on both private methods are already present from implementation. 28/28 tests pass.
